I never went to school. I learned everything from my mother and from watching the neighbors with my own eyes. I have been in the fields since before I could carry a full bucket, and now I manage our 8 mu. I put 6 mu into wheat and then maize because we need to fill our own bellies. The other 2 mu I plant cotton so we have cash for salt, oil, and school fees for the little ones.

Last year my wheat got about 450 kg each mu, and this year I will do the same thing. I sow the improved wheat seed that Old Zhang used — his wheat stood taller and heavier than mine. Before sowing last autumn, I rotavated the land. Now I will irrigate three times: when the wheat turns green and wakes up, when the stems shoot up, and when the heads are filling. I spread one big 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer on every mu as base, and then I topdress with urea two times. Better to put a bit too much than too little. Wasting fertilizer costs money, but a bad harvest means my children go hungry.

After we cut the wheat in June, there is no time to rest. I plant hybrid maize seed the same day or the next morning, using the no-till machine that drills straight into the wheat stubble. I learned this from watching everyone in the village — if you stop to plough, you miss the rain window and the season is lost. The maize gets water three times and spray two times. I put compound fertilizer down at planting and urea later when it is knee-high.

Cotton is on my south plot, 2 mu. I plough that land deep because cotton roots need loose soil to go down. I plant hybrid cotton seed in April. Cotton needs water two times, but the bugs love it more than I do, so I spray five times. Last year the bollworms came early and chewed half the buds before I caught them. The dealer sells me the spray — I know the red bottle and the blue bottle, that is enough.

My husband and his brother work in the city when construction jobs come, so for cotton picking I hire two women from the village to help. But for spraying and watering, I do it myself with my mother. I do not change what works. Everyone around here uses about this much seed, fertilizer, and water, so I do the same. Spending money on extra fertilizer hurts, but losing the whole crop is a disaster I cannot face.
